mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3% annualized over a 6-month horizon signals accelerating demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 exceeds 3% but S&P 500 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% over 3 months signals tight labor markets, which historically leads to wage pressures and higher corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% and stays below for 3 months
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% but S&P 500 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% over 3 months signals monetary tightening, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise and corporate earnings expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5% and stays above for 3 months
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% but S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.
